name: Signal vs. noise
originator: Norbert Wiener / Claude Shannon (signal theory); statistics of multiple testing
rule: Random data is full of apparent patterns. A real pattern predicts new data it wasn't fitted to, so beware overfitting and testing many hypotheses at once.
plain: If you look at enough things, some will look meaningful by accident. Real patterns keep working on fresh data.
formula: P(at least one false hit) = 1 − (1 − α)^k  → with α = 0.05, k = 20: ≈ 64%

story.beat: Rook's crew checked 20 factors and found oxygen dips on Tuesdays. 'It's the Tuesday mining shift!' You scatter 20 random dot-clouds on the wall, and one of them also shows a 'Tuesday effect'. With 20 tries, a fluke is likely. Next week's Tuesday is normal, and the pattern vanishes.

examples.text: A trader finds a 'winning rule' by testing 500 rules on last year's prices. On this year's prices it loses.
A cluster of 4 headaches in one corridor looks alarming, but with 40 corridors, one cluster is expected by chance.
'Every time I wash my suit, a dust storm comes.' You remember the hits and forget the misses.

sim.try: Reshuffle a few times and count the 'patterns' in pure noise. Then retest the flagged ones on new data.

realCase.title: The dead salmon fMRI study
realCase.text: Researchers put a dead salmon in a brain scanner and 'asked' it to judge emotions in photos. Without correcting for the thousands of brain regions tested, some regions lit up as 'active'. The spoof study showed how multiple comparisons manufacture signals from noise.
realCase.source: Bennett, Baird, Miller & Wolford, poster at Human Brain Mapping (2009); J. Serendipitous & Unexpected Results (2010)

misuse: Dismissing every surprising pattern as noise. Real early signals exist; the answer is to test them on new data, not to ignore them.
sources: John Ioannidis, 'Why Most Published Research Findings Are False', PLoS Medicine (2005)
Nate Silver, The Signal and the Noise (2012)

predict.prompt: You test 20 unrelated factors at the 5% level. Chance at least one looks 'significant' by luck?

options: Test the pattern on data it wasn't built from
mcq.why: Out-of-sample prediction separates signal from noise.

whichModel.prompt: A fund shows its best strategy out of 1,000 it backtested, and it fails once live.
whichModel.why: Picking the best of many fits is overfitting.
